This Mfa Is Filed U/S 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 02/11/2016 Passed In Mvc
No.5437/2014 On The File Of Xiii Addl.

Small Cause
Judge And Member Mact, Bengaluru (Scch-15), Partly
Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And
Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal Coming On For Hearing This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 1 and 3.

This appeal is directed against the judgment and award in MVC No.5437/2014 by XIII Additional Small Causes Judge and Member MACT, Bengaluru, whereby, the appellant/petitioner was awarded a sum of `4,96,200/- for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident by partly allowing the claim petition.

entities.text: XIII Additional Small Causes Judge and Member MACT, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The brief facts are as below:

The petitioner contended that on 10.12.2014 at about 11.30 a.m., petitioner and other inmates were traveling in a K.S.R.T.C., bus bearing Regn.No.KA-42-F-252 on NH- 209, Kanakapura-Bengaluru main road and when said bus reached near Jain College, a tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-42-151 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction and took to extreme right side of the road and dashed against the KSRTC bus.

In the result, petitioner has sustained injury, namely, lacerated wound over the antero lateral aspect of right proximal tibial area and deformity, swelling restriction of right lower limb movements and fracture of right proximal tibia.
He was taken to hospital.
A case was registered by Harohalli Traffic police in Cr.No.418/2014 against the driver of the tipper lorry.

sentences.text: The petitioner contended that due to injury sustained by him he has suffered permanent disablement NC: 2023:KHC:20974 and he was aged 33 years and working as Supervisor at Kanakapura Quarry and earning a sum of `18,000/-p.m.
After the accident the petitioner is not able to attend his work.
Petitioner has already spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
The respondent No.2 is the RC owner of tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-42-151 and respondent No.1 is the insurer of the said vehicle and respondent No.3 is the owner of KSRTC bus.
Hence, all the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, petitioner prays to allow the claim petition.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 appeared before the Tribunal through their counsel and the owner of the tipper lorry did not appear despite service of notice.

Respondent No.1 i.e. the insurer of the tipper lorry contended that though the insurance policy issued by it was in force at the time of the accident, there were serious violations of the terms and conditions of the policy and that the vehicle did not have a valid permit and driver did not have a valid driving license and therefore, denied the liability.
NC: 2023:KHC:20974 5.
Respondent No.3-KSRTC contended that the driver of the bus was in no way responsible for the alleged accident and therefore, the liability has to be fastened upon the respondent Nos. 1 and 2.

Inter alia, both the respondents contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant,
imaginary and untenable and they denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
6. The Tribunal on the above pleadings framed necessary issues and the petitioner was examined as PW1 and Exs.P1 to P20 were marked.
The petitioner also examined two witnesses as PWs 2 and 3.
Respondent No.2 examined its driver as RW1 and copy of the insurance policy is marked and respondent No.1 has examined its officer as RW2 and Ex.R1 to 6 were marked.

The Investigating Officer was examined as RW3 and ARTO was examined as RW1.
7.

After hearing both the sides, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the tipper lorry was not having a valid permit at the time of the accident and therefore, liability of NC: 2023:KHC:20974 the insurance company is to be absolved and as such, fastened the liability on the respondent No.2-owner and proceeded to award the compensation of `4,96,200/-under different heads as below:
 Pain and sufferings ` 30,000/-
 Loss of past earnings ` 14,000/-
 7000 x2 =14000  Medical expenditure `3,60,000/-
 Loss of future income ` 67,200/-
 Towards diet and conveyance ` 15,000/-
 Loss of amenities ` 10,000/-
 Total `4,96,200/-

sentences.text: 8. Aggrieved by the said judgment, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal contending that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is not proper and it is abysmally low.

It is also contended that the Tribunal erred in fastening the liability on the owner of the lorry and therefore, appropriate finding may be given in this regard.
9.
On issuance of notice, respondent Nos. 1 and 3 appeared before this Court through their counsel and respondent No.2 did not appear despite service of notice.
NC: 2023:KHC:20974 On admitting the appeal, the Tribunal records have been secured.
10. The arguments by learned counsel for respondent Nos. 1 and 3 were heard and counsel for the appellant did not appear to advance his arguments.
11. The grievance of the appellant as may be found from the appeal memo is in respect of the quantum of the compensation and the liability being fastened upon the respondent No.2
It was contended that the compensation awarded is abysmally low and not commensurate with the injuries suffered by him and as such, there is a need for enhancement.

12. The learned counsel for respondent No.1 in his submissions, contended that the Tribunal has considered the liability in proper perspective and the absence of the permit for the driver of the tipper lorry had been established by the evidence on record and therefore, the Tribunal has rightly absolved the liability of respondent NC: 2023:KHC:20974 No.1.
Therefore, he contended that the quantum of compensation is also proper and correct.

13. A perusal of the impugned judgment as well as the Tribunal records would indicate that the evidence of ARTO, who was examined as RW4, has categorically states that the said lorry bearing No. KA 42-151 had got permit from his office for period 26-2-2009 to 25-2-2014 and produced the same as per Ex.R5.
Evidently, the accident had occurred on 10-12-2014 which is about eight months later to the expiry of the permit.
Therefore, it is evident that the lorry did not possess the permit as on the date of the accident.
14. Respondent No.2 being the owner of the Lorry has not led any evidence and did not produce any documents which would rebut the Ex.R5.
Therefore, it is clear that as on the date of the accident, the tipper lorry was not having the valid permit.

The Tribunal relying on the decision in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs Challa Bharathamma1 fastened liability on the respondent No.2.
16.

sentences.text: "it does not require the wisdom of the "Tripitaka", that the existence of a permit of any nature is a matter of documentary evidence.
Nothing has been brought on record by the insured to prove that he had a permit of the vehicle.
In such a situation, the onus cannot be cast on the insurer.

Therefore, the tribunal as well as the High Court had directed the insurer was required to pay the compensation amount to the claimants with interest with the stipulation that the insurer shall be entitled to recover the same from the owner and the driver."

17. The discussion of the Apex court preceded to the above observation in the penultimate paragraph of the judgment shows that absence of the permit as on the date 2004 ACJ 2094 (2018)2 SCC 558 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:20974 of the accident cannot be equated to the absence of the insurance policy or absence licence.
But it is only infraction.
Therefore, in the case on hand also, respondent No.1-Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and then recover the same from respondent No.2-owner of the tipper lorry.

18. Coming to the quantum of the compensation, it is evident that the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the petitioner at `7,000/- per month in the absence of any cogent and valid documentary evidence on record.
The accident had taken place in the year 2014.
The guidelines issued by the KSLSA for settlement of disputes before the Lok Adalat prescribe notional income at Rs.8,500/- per month for the year 2014.
In umpteen number of decisions, this Court has held that such guidelines issued by KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken at `8,500/- per month.
The Tribunal has held that PW3 says the disability of the petitioner at 17%, but it is on the higher side.
The functional disability of the petitioner is considered to be at 5%.
It is relevant to note that the petitioner has sustained lacerated wound over the antero lateral aspect of right proximal tibial area; and it was diagnosed to be the fracture of right tibia.
Therefore, the said injuries having been treated, I do not find any reason to hold that the functional disability of the petitioner is to be assessed more.
20. As a result, the compensation under the head of loss of future income is calculated as: `8500 x 12 x 16 x 5%=`81,600/-.
Consequently, the loss of earning during the laid up period is also to be revised.
It can be safely be held that the petitioner as unable to resume his work for a period of three months.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for `25,500/-.

21. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of `30,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings,

towards loss of amenities.

sentences.text: Except loss of amenities, all other compensation are proper and correct.
22. The petitioner is aged 33 years and he has to live with the disability for the rest of his life.

Therefore, the loss of amenities is to be enhanced from `10,000/- to `20,000/-.
23.

Therefore, the compensation is reassessed by this Court and the petitioner is entitled for additional compensation of `35,900/-under different heads as below:
 Pain and sufferings ` 30,000/-
 Loss of income during laid up ` 25,500/-
 period  8500 x3 =25500

Medical expenditure `3,60,000/-

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for enhanced compensation of `35,900/- with interest and therefore, the - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:20974 appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified holding that respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the Tipper lorry and by awarding a sum of `35,900/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.

(iii) The respondent No.1 -Insurance Company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order and is at liberty to recover the said amount from Sri Jay Prakash @ Jai Prakash Choudhary vs The Manager on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118567856/
